title: PCNA-RECQL5-RPRD1B recruit repair components to stressed replication forks to promote survival of BRCA1-deficient cancer cells.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all 16 Figshare zips via the Figshare application programming interface (API) and downloaded 5 of the small ones (FIGURE 3, 4, 6, 7, 8); unzipped and listed every file; opened all 11 Excel (.xlsx) files found inside with openpyxl and printed sheet names, dimensions and first rows. Also unzipped the Nucleic Acids Research supplement and extracted the text of both Word (.docx) files. Checked the Mendeley link with a HTTP HEAD request.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Which assay produced each figure panel (described in the Supplementary Extended Methods), and the contents of the 5 large zips (FIGURE 1, 5, SUPPLEMENTAL 1, 2, 3, 6; 25-81 MB each) which I did not download — their names indicate they hold the same mix of western blot and confocal image files as the small ones.

a1_downloadable.note: Figshare deposit (16 zips, CC BY 4.0) downloads without login; I pulled 5 zips successfully. The second link in the data availability statement, https://data.mendeley.com/preview/h92sg7rnkj, is a private pre-publication preview URL and returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no feature/label table anywhere. The deposit is raw western blot TIFF images plus 11 small Excel files of per-figure densitometry laid out as formatted chart-source blocks (merged cells, no header row, data starting at arbitrary cells like D6 or C4). Any prediction target would have to be constructed by hand from blot images and figure legends.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No model inputs exist. There are no sequences, structures, expression matrices or compound structures; inputs would be uncropped gel images and confocal micrographs with no accompanying annotation, segmentation mask or per-object metadata file.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL. Densitometry values are bare integers (e.g. 2113, 14501) in arbitrary band-intensity units with no units column, alongside unlabelled 'normalization' columns. The one ImageJ measurement export (DNA fiber ratio raw data.xlsx) has Area/Mean/Length columns with no units given anywhere.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Largest usable table is the 'combined ratios' sheet of DNA fiber ratio raw data.xlsx: 493 fiber-tract ratios across exactly 2 conditions (siControl vs siRPRD1B at 60 min). Everything else is n = 3 replicate triplets per panel; fork data.xlsx is a 4-column by 3-row contingency table of stalled/restarted/new forks. Far below the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~350 MB total across all 16 Figshare zips
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem; the whole deposit fits easily on a laptop. The largest single file seen is a 54 MB blot TIFF inside FIGURE 8.zip.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: What I opened is consistent with the paper: replicate counts in the Excel sheets (3 rows per condition) match the 'n = 3' stated in the supplementary figure legends, and the fiber counts are the same order as the '>100 fibers' phrasing.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean where values exist — all numbers trace to physical measurements (blot densitometry, confocal foci counts, DNA fiber tract lengths measured in ImageJ). No model-derived or predicted columns. A8 is not the reason this fails.

existing_models.name: DNAi (open-source deep-learning tool for DNA fiber image analysis, Nucleic Acids Research 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report it matches trained human graders on segmentation and fiber-length measurement and runs about 30x faster than manual annotation; trained on a large set of hand-annotated fiber images. Exact split not checked by me.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not read in detail — I only retrieved the abstract-level description, since this paper's data cannot support such a project anyway.

existing_models.name: FiberAI (deep-learning detector for nascent DNA fibers, bioRxiv 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported bounding-box average precision 0.91 and segmentation average precision 0.90 on their own microscopy images; split not stated in what I retrieved.

backbone.name: none applicable
backbone.licence: Figshare deposit is CC BY 4.0, which would permit reuse — but there is nothing modellable to reuse.

integration.join_key: none — the deposit contains no standard identifiers (no UniProt accessions, Ensembl gene IDs or genomic coordinates), only gene symbols typed into spreadsheet labels
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with 3 replicates per condition and no identifier column, there is nothing to join a large resource to.

controls.positive_control: None available in this data. The paper's own internal controls (siControl vs siRPRD1B) are experiment design, not an ML positive control.
controls.negative_control: Not runnable — label shuffling needs labels, and there are none.
controls.external_validation: None. The global microRNA (miR) microarray behind Supplementary Figure 1A is described as done 'as previously described' and has no Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) or ArrayExpress accession anywhere in the text or the text-mined accession list.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: the deposited data is figure-source material (blot images and triplicate densitometry) with no feature matrix, no label column and no replicate structure beyond n = 3, so any model trained on it would be describing three measurements per condition.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use replication-fork and blot measurements to predict which cells with a broken BRCA1 gene die when a repair scaffold is removed.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would have used the per-cell DNA fiber tract measurements and band-intensity readouts as features. In the files there are 493 fiber ratios in 2 conditions and 3 replicates per blot panel — nowhere near enough examples.
plain_idea.predict: Cell survival or repair efficiency after knocking down RPRD1B, a protein that scaffolds repair of broken replication forks. The true answer comes from colony-formation assays and microscope-counted repair foci, both read off images by hand.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: DNA-repair labs hunting for drug targets in BRCA1-mutant breast and ovarian cancer would want a model that ranks scaffold proteins by how lethal their loss is. This dataset cannot support that; it is a single mechanism story, not a screen.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The nearest idea — a deep-learning segmenter for DNA fiber spreading images — is already served by DNAi and FiberAI, and this deposit contributes no annotated fiber images to it (only one ImageJ measurement export, already measured). The underlying biological question, ranking synthetic-lethal partners of BRCA1 loss, needs a screen-scale resource such as DepMap, not this paper's eight figures.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated because no feature table can be built. The 0.35 GB working set is the sum of the 16 Figshare zip sizes reported by the Figshare application programming interface.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open any one of the per-figure Excel files and count the rows — it takes two minutes and shows n = 3 replicates in a formatted chart block with no header row. I did this for all 11 and it killed the project.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A on A2, A3, A4 and A5, all verified by opening the files. This is a wet-lab mechanism paper whose entire deposit is figure-source material: uncropped western blot TIFFs, confocal images, and 11 small Excel files of densitometry formatted as chart inputs (merged cells, no header row, bare intensity integers with no units). The single biggest table is 493 DNA fiber ratios across 2 conditions; everything else is n = 3. There is no label column, no input matrix and no standard identifier to join on, so a prediction target would have to be built by hand from images. The Mendeley half of the data availability statement is a private preview URL returning HTTP 401. Nothing here is salvageable for machine learning, and the one adjacent task (automated DNA fiber image analysis) already has two open tools, DNAi and FiberAI.
